transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess the main thing is my sleep has gotten really messed up lately. Like, I’ll get into bed and I’m tired, or at least I think I should be tired, but then my mind just keeps going and going and I end up staying up half the night. And other times I do fall asleep, but then I wake up way too early, like before I’m supposed to, and I just feel like I never really rested at all.

It’s been getting frustrating because I don’t feel like I’m starting the day normally anymore. I’m either lying there for hours waiting to fall asleep, or I’m awake too early and already exhausted. That’s mostly why I came in.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

Yeah… I have. I mean, I don’t know exactly how to explain it without sounding dramatic, but lately I wake up and there’s this heavy, empty feeling already there, like before anything has even happened that day. It’s like I open my eyes and I’m already weighed down.

And it’s strange because I’ll be sitting in my own condo — the place I worked really hard to get, and I used to feel proud of it — and instead of feeling comfortable or happy or anything, I just feel like I might cry. Sometimes I look around and think, “This should feel good, I should feel okay here,” but it just doesn’t. It feels kind of hollow, like I’m there but not really connected to it. So… yeah, sad and down, definitely.
How long have you been feeling this heavy, empty feeling?

I’d say it’s been around for about five months, maybe a little more if I’m being honest. It wasn’t like one morning I woke up and everything was suddenly terrible, it was more like this fog started settling in and I kept thinking it would lift if I just got through the week, or caught up on things, or stopped overthinking.

But it’s been hanging around for months now — this depressed, guilty kind of feeling. And it definitely got worse after I bought the condo, which sounds backwards because that was supposed to be a good thing. I thought I’d feel proud or relieved, like I was moving forward, but instead it got heavier. So… about five months, with the worst of it more recently after the condo.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I have. That’s actually been one of the weirder parts, because it’s not like I made some decision to stop doing things. It’s more like I just… don’t feel anything toward them anymore.

I used to go to salsa class, and I really liked it. It gave me something to look forward to, and I liked being around people there even if I wasn’t the best dancer or anything. But I just stopped going. At first I told myself I was just skipping one class, then it became another one, and then I kind of stopped even pretending I was going back.

And painting too… I have my paints still sitting out on the table at home. They’ve just been there, like I left them expecting I’d pick them up again, but I’ll look at them and feel nothing. It’s almost like they belong to somebody else, which sounds strange, but that’s how it feels. Like I remember that I used to care about it, but I can’t really access that feeling right now.
Have you experienced any periods where you felt significantly better over the past five months?

Yeah… there were a few stretches where I felt really different, like almost weirdly better. Earlier this month especially, I remember feeling kind of lit up, like I had this energy or confidence that I hadn’t had in a while. Not just “a little less depressed,” but more like I suddenly felt unstoppable, like I could handle everything and maybe I’d been making too big a deal out of how bad I’d been feeling.

But it didn’t exactly feel peaceful, if that makes sense. It was like I was turned up too high. And then little things would set me off. My mom would ask me some normal question, like if I’d eaten or if I’d called someone back, and I’d snap at her like she was criticizing me. Or at work, my supervisor would ask a small follow-up question about something, nothing major, and I’d feel this flash of irritation, like, “Why are you questioning me?” even though normally I don’t think that would bother me that much.

So yes, I guess there have been times I felt significantly better, but not in a calm, steady way. More like suddenly really up and then kind of sharp with people.
Have you been experiencing these mood swings frequently over the past five months?

I wouldn’t say it’s been the whole five months in that really obvious back-and-forth way. The low feeling has been there for months, but the actual cycling — like being really charged up and then crashing down again — that’s been much more recent.

Probably about a month? It started feeling noticeable once the mortgage became real, like after the condo stopped being this abstract “I’m buying a place” thing and became… this huge permanent responsibility. Since then it’s felt more like I swing between getting this burst of energy or confidence, and then dropping back into this heavy crash. Before that, I think I was mostly just down. But the noticeable ups and downs have been about a month.
Have you ever had a period where you didn't need to sleep, or where you felt like you could go without sleep for an extended time?

Yeah… that has happened. Not like I was trying to pull an all-nighter or anything, but there were several nights where I only slept maybe three or four hours, and then I’d wake up feeling strangely charged.

Normally if I sleep that little, I’m useless the next day — like I need coffee immediately and I’m dragging myself around. But during those nights, I’d get up and feel like I didn’t even need coffee, like my body was already running on something. It felt almost confusing, because part of me knew, “You barely slept, you should be exhausted,” but I just wasn’t. I’d be awake and alert really quickly, like I was ready to start doing things.
When you're feeling really up or charged, do you ever feel like you're capable of doing anything or that you're more important than usual?

Yeah… I think so. It’s embarrassing to say out loud because now it sounds kind of unrealistic, but when I’m in that charged-up place, I really do start thinking like I can handle anything if I just push hard enough.

Like with the condo, I wasn’t just thinking, “Okay, I can manage the payments.” I was thinking I could somehow pay it down really fast, like way faster than would probably make sense on my income. And then I’d start stacking other things on top of that in my head, like, “I should just study for the CPA exams, I could pass them, and I could start a little bookkeeping business on the side too.” It all felt completely possible at the time, like failure wasn’t even part of the equation.

It wasn’t like I thought I was famous or anything like that, but I definitely felt more capable than usual. More… important, maybe, or like I was finally seeing how much I could do and everyone else was just underestimating me. Then later, when I’m not in that mood, I look at it and think, “That was a lot. Where did that confidence even come from?”
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people couldn't hear or see when you were feeling really up or charged?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve definitely had moments where my thoughts are going really fast and I’m reading into things more than I normally would, but I haven’t heard voices like someone talking to me when nobody’s there.

And I haven’t seen things either, not like seeing a person or something that other people couldn’t see. Sometimes when I’m really keyed up I might feel more alert to sounds or notice stuff more intensely, like every little noise stands out, but I don’t think I’ve had anything where I’d say I was hearing or seeing something that wasn’t real.
When you're feeling really up or charged, do you find yourself taking on more projects or activities than you normally would?

Yes, definitely. That’s actually one of the things I notice more clearly afterward, because in the moment it feels productive, like I’m just finally getting my life together.

I’ll come home from work and instead of just making dinner or watching something, I’ll start cleaning like the whole place needs to be fixed right then. Not just regular cleaning either — I mean pulling things out of cabinets, reorganizing stuff, making piles, wiping down things I usually ignore. And while I’m doing that, I’ll be making renovation lists in my head or on my phone, like what I’d change in the kitchen, what flooring would cost, what I could paint myself, what I’d need a contractor for.

Then I’d switch over to checking interest rates or mortgage calculators, just clicking around and comparing numbers like it was urgent. And then somehow that would turn into side-job ideas, like setting up bookkeeping work on the side, figuring out what I’d charge, what kind of clients I could get, making lists of business names or little plans.

It’s like after work, when normally I should be tired, I’d get this burst of energy and keep stacking things on. Cleaning, lists, money stuff, side-job planning — all in the same night sometimes. And I couldn’t really shut it off. Even if I told myself, “Okay, stop, just go sit down,” I’d think of one more thing I had to look up or write down.
When you're feeling really up or charged, do you feel like you're invincible or that nothing can go wrong?

Yeah… not invincible exactly, like I didn’t think I could walk into traffic or something dramatic like that. But I did have this feeling like things couldn’t really fail if I just pushed hard enough.

Like I honestly started thinking I could buy the condo and pay it down really fast, even though when I’m calmer I can see that was probably not realistic for my income. And at the same time I was thinking, “I’ll just study for the CPA exams, I can pass them,” and then also, “I could run a bookkeeping business on the side.” It wasn’t just daydreaming, it felt like a plan, like of course I could do all of it.

So maybe not “nothing can go wrong” in those exact words, but failure just didn’t feel like an option in my head. I kind of brushed past the risks, like they were details I’d figure out later.
When you're feeling really up or charged, do you ever do things that might be considered reckless or impulsive, like spending a lot of money or acting out of character?

I’m not sure I’d call it reckless, exactly. I don’t think I’ve done anything really extreme or dangerous, like… I’m not going out and doing wild things completely unlike me.

The closest thing would probably be getting really caught up in money plans or future plans and feeling like I should act on them faster than I normally would. Like I might spend way too much time looking at costs or options and feel tempted to make a big decision, but I usually don’t fully go through with something huge. Or if I buy things, it’s more like things for a project or organizing or improving my place, not like I’m suddenly buying a car or gambling or something.

So… impulsive in my thinking, maybe? Like I get ahead of myself and everything feels urgent. But I don’t know if my actual behavior has crossed into what other people would call reckless. I guess I’d have to think about that more.
Have you done anything impulsive that doesn't involve money, like quitting a job, ending a relationship, or doing something spontaneous that's out of character for you?

I don’t think so… at least not in a big, obvious way like quitting my job or suddenly ending a relationship. I haven’t had one of those moments where I just blow up my life and then later I’m like, “What did I do?”

I guess when I’m in that state, I can feel very ready to make decisions, like I’ll think, “I should just change everything,” or I’ll get this strong urge to start over or fix things immediately. But when it comes to actually doing something like walking out of work or cutting someone off completely, I don’t think I’ve really done that.

Sometimes I might say things more quickly or make plans that are kind of intense for me, like deciding I’m going to completely reorganize my schedule or take on some big personal project, but I usually don’t follow through with something irreversible. So… no, I don’t think I’ve quit a job or ended a relationship impulsively. If there are smaller things, I may not be recognizing them as impulsive, but nothing major comes to mind.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or irritable for several days in a row?

Yeah… yes, I think so. Earlier this month there was a stretch where I felt almost, like, lit up from the inside. Not just in a good mood, but charged, like I had this extra engine running and everything felt more possible than usual.

And it wasn’t all happy, exactly. It would kind of flip into being really irritated. Like my mom would ask me a normal question, something small, and I’d snap back like she was getting in my way. Or my supervisor would ask me to clarify something at work, and I’d feel this burst of annoyance, like, “Why are you questioning me?” even though normally I’d just answer and move on.

It lasted several days, yeah. It wasn’t just one afternoon where I had coffee or got good news. It was more like a few days in a row where I felt unstoppable, and then over little things I’d get sharp with people in a way that didn’t really fit the situation.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or elevated for several days in a row, without any apparent reason?

Yeah… I think that’s what I was trying to describe. Earlier this month, there were several days where I felt really elevated for no clear reason. Like nothing major had happened that would explain it — I hadn’t gotten some amazing news or anything — but I just felt kind of lit up, like I had this sense that I could handle everything and that I was almost unstoppable.

It wasn’t just “I’m having a nice day,” either. It felt bigger than that, like my mood was turned up too high. And at first it almost felt good, because I was more confident and energized in my head, but then it would switch really quickly into irritation. Like my mom would ask me a normal question, something that shouldn’t have bothered me at all, and I’d snap at her. Or my supervisor would ask me to clarify something, and I’d feel this immediate annoyance, like they were getting in my way or questioning me, even though normally I’d just answer.

So yes, it did feel elevated for several days, and I don’t think there was an obvious reason for it. It kind of came on like this charged feeling, and then I was more reactive than usual.
Do you think anything in particular triggers these mood swings of feeling really up or charged, and then crashing back down?

I think the biggest thing I can point to is the mortgage. Like, once that became real — not just an idea or something we were talking about in the future, but actually real — that’s when I started noticing the more obvious cycling.

It’s been about a month, I’d say. Before that, I’m sure I had moods, obviously, but this more noticeable pattern of feeling really charged up and then coming back down hard… that seems like it started around then. It’s like my brain latched onto it as this huge life thing, and since then I’ve been going up and down in a way that feels much more obvious to me.

So I don’t know if it’s the only trigger, but that’s the main one I can identify. The mortgage becoming real feels like the point where this all got louder.
Have you experienced any periods of at least four consecutive days where you felt abnormally happy, irritable, or energetic?

Yes. Earlier this month, there was definitely a stretch like that — at least several days in a row — where I felt… I don’t know, almost lit up. Like I had this extra push in me and I could do anything, or handle everything, and I remember thinking I felt kind of unstoppable.

But it wasn’t just happy in a simple way. It also had this edge to it. I’d get irritated really fast over things that normally wouldn’t even register. Like my mom would ask me a small question, just normal stuff, and I’d snap at her like she was bothering me. Or at work, if my supervisor asked me to clarify something, I’d feel immediately annoyed, like they were criticizing me or slowing me down, even though looking back they were just asking a basic question.

So yes, it did last for several days, and it felt noticeably different from my normal mood.

Yes, that did happen. During that stretch I was talking about, there were several nights where I only slept maybe three or four hours, which is really not much for me, and then I’d still get up feeling strangely charged.

It wasn’t like when you sleep badly and you’re dragging the next day and need a bunch of coffee just to function. It was almost the opposite. I’d wake up and feel like I was already switched on, like coffee wasn’t even necessary. I remember thinking it was weird because I knew I hadn’t slept enough, but my body didn’t feel like it was catching up to that. It was more like I was running on this internal energy, and I didn’t feel tired in the normal way.
Have you had a period of at least two weeks where you felt depressed or lost interest in activities nearly every day?

Yes… lately I have been feeling depressed, pretty much most days. I don’t know if I can neatly measure it, but it feels like I wake up and there’s already this heavy, empty feeling sitting in my chest before anything has even happened.

And the weirdest part is, I’ll be sitting in my own condo — something I worked so hard for, something I thought was supposed to make me feel proud or settled — and instead I just feel like crying. Like I’ll look around and think, “This should feel good, I should be happy here,” but it doesn’t land that way. It just feels heavy and kind of hollow.

So yes, there has been a stretch where it feels like that nearly every day.
Have these mood swings and periods of high energy caused problems for you at work, in relationships, or in other areas of your life?

Yes… it has. I mean, I’m still getting to work, so from the outside I probably look like I’m functioning okay, but I don’t feel like I’m doing as well as I should be.

At work, I’ve made mistakes I normally don’t make, especially with reconciliations. Like I’ll think I’m being really productive or that I’m catching everything, and then later there’ll be numbers that don’t line up, or I’ll realize I missed something obvious. It happened enough that my supervisor actually pulled me aside to talk about it, which was embarrassing because I’m usually pretty careful with that stuff. That’s kind of the part of my job where I’m supposed to be reliable.

And outside work, I’ve been pulling back from people. I used to go to salsa class, and I haven’t been going. I keep making excuses or just not responding because I don’t feel like myself, and I don’t want people noticing or asking what’s wrong. Same with friends — I’ll avoid plans, even if part of me knows seeing them might help. It just feels like too much to show up and pretend I’m normal.

And then I’d start stacking other things on top of that in my head, like, “I should just study for the CPA exams, I could pass them, and I could start a little bookkeeping business on the side too.” It all felt completely possible at the time, like failure wasn’t even part of the equation.

It wasn’t like I thought I was famous or anything like that, but I definitely felt more capable than usual. More… important, maybe, or like I was finally seeing how much I could do and everyone else was just underestimating me. Then later, when I’m not in that mood, I look at it and think, “That was a lot. Where did that confidence even come from?”

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of psychotic symptoms
doctor.question: Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people couldn't hear or see when you were feeling really up or charged?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about hallucinations or psychotic symptoms during an up/charged mood, but the provided symptom profile does not include hallucinations or psychosis.

patient.answer:
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve definitely had moments where my thoughts are going really fast and I’m reading into things more than I normally would, but I haven’t heard voices like someone talking to me when nobody’s there.

And I haven’t seen things either, not like seeing a person or something that other people couldn’t see. Sometimes when I’m really keyed up I might feel more alert to sounds or notice stuff more intensely, like every little noise stands out, but I don’t think I’ve had anything where I’d say I was hearing or seeing something that wasn’t real.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of increased goal-directed activity when feeling charged or up
doctor.question: When you're feeling really up or charged, do you find yourself taking on more projects or activities than you normally would?

target_item.name: Increased_Activity
target_item.manifestation: For a while I had this burst of energy where I was cleaning, making renovation lists, checking interest rates, and setting up side-job ideas all after work like I couldn’t shut it off.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether, during charged-up periods, I take on more projects or activities than usual, which directly matches increased activity and goal-directed energy.

patient.answer:
Yes, definitely. That’s actually one of the things I notice more clearly afterward, because in the moment it feels productive, like I’m just finally getting my life together.

I’ll come home from work and instead of just making dinner or watching something, I’ll start cleaning like the whole place needs to be fixed right then. Not just regular cleaning either — I mean pulling things out of cabinets, reorganizing stuff, making piles, wiping down things I usually ignore. And while I’m doing that, I’ll be making renovation lists in my head or on my phone, like what I’d change in the kitchen, what flooring would cost, what I could paint myself, what I’d need a contractor for.

Then I’d switch over to checking interest rates or mortgage calculators, just clicking around and comparing numbers like it was urgent. And then somehow that would turn into side-job ideas, like setting up bookkeeping work on the side, figuring out what I’d charge, what kind of clients I could get, making lists of business names or little plans.

It’s like after work, when normally I should be tired, I’d get this burst of energy and keep stacking things on. Cleaning, lists, money stuff, side-job planning — all in the same night sometimes. And I couldn’t really shut it off. Even if I told myself, “Okay, stop, just go sit down,” I’d think of one more thing I had to look up or write down.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of increased self-esteem during manic episodes
doctor.question: When you're feeling really up or charged, do you feel like you're invincible or that nothing can go wrong?

target_item.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
target_item.manifestation: I honestly started thinking I could pay the condo down fast, pass the CPA exams, and run a little bookkeeping business on the side like failure just wasn’t an option.
target_item.reason: The question is directly asking about feeling invincible or overly confident during an up or charged mood, which matches inflated self-esteem or grandiosity.

patient.answer:
Yeah… not invincible exactly, like I didn’t think I could walk into traffic or something dramatic like that. But I did have this feeling like things couldn’t really fail if I just pushed hard enough.

Like I honestly started thinking I could buy the condo and pay it down really fast, even though when I’m calmer I can see that was probably not realistic for my income. And at the same time I was thinking, “I’ll just study for the CPA exams, I can pass them,” and then also, “I could run a bookkeeping business on the side.” It wasn’t just daydreaming, it felt like a plan, like of course I could do all of it.

So maybe not “nothing can go wrong” in those exact words, but failure just didn’t feel like an option in my head. I kind of brushed past the risks, like they were details I’d figure out later.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of reckless behavior during manic episodes
doctor.question: When you're feeling really up or charged, do you ever do things that might be considered reckless or impulsive, like spending a lot of money or acting out of character?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about reckless or impulsive behavior/risk-taking during an up or charged period, but the provided symptom profile does not include a specific item covering risky activities, impulsive spending, or acting out of character.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure I’d call it reckless, exactly. I don’t think I’ve done anything really extreme or dangerous, like… I’m not going out and doing wild things completely unlike me.

The closest thing would probably be getting really caught up in money plans or future plans and feeling like I should act on them faster than I normally would. Like I might spend way too much time looking at costs or options and feel tempted to make a big decision, but I usually don’t fully go through with something huge. Or if I buy things, it’s more like things for a project or organizing or improving my place, not like I’m suddenly buying a car or gambling or something.

So… impulsive in my thinking, maybe? Like I get ahead of myself and everything feels urgent. But I don’t know if my actual behavior has crossed into what other people would call reckless. I guess I’d have to think about that more.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's reckless or impulsive behavior is limited to spending money or if it extends to other areas
doctor.question: Have you done anything impulsive that doesn't involve money, like quitting a job, ending a relationship, or doing something spontaneous that's out of character for you?

target_item.reason: The question asks specifically about impulsive or risky behaviors outside of money, such as quitting a job or ending a relationship, but the provided symptom profile does not include a distinct item for reckless or impulsive non-financial behavior.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so… at least not in a big, obvious way like quitting my job or suddenly ending a relationship. I haven’t had one of those moments where I just blow up my life and then later I’m like, “What did I do?”

I guess when I’m in that state, I can feel very ready to make decisions, like I’ll think, “I should just change everything,” or I’ll get this strong urge to start over or fix things immediately. But when it comes to actually doing something like walking out of work or cutting someone off completely, I don’t think I’ve really done that.

Sometimes I might say things more quickly or make plans that are kind of intense for me, like deciding I’m going to completely reorganize my schedule or take on some big personal project, but I usually don’t follow through with something irreversible. So… no, I don’t think I’ve quit a job or ended a relationship impulsively. If there are smaller things, I may not be recognizing them as impulsive, but nothing major comes to mind.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's mood swings are a result of a bipolar disorder
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or irritable for several days in a row?

target_item.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Earlier in the month I felt almost lit up and unstoppable, then I’d snap at my mom or my supervisor over little questions that normally wouldn’t bother me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about episodes of unusually elevated or irritable mood lasting several days, which directly matches this symptom.

patient.answer:
Yeah… yes, I think so. Earlier this month there was a stretch where I felt almost, like, lit up from the inside. Not just in a good mood, but charged, like I had this extra engine running and everything felt more possible than usual.

And it wasn’t all happy, exactly. It would kind of flip into being really irritated. Like my mom would ask me a normal question, something small, and I’d snap back like she was getting in my way. Or my supervisor would ask me to clarify something at work, and I’d feel this burst of annoyance, like, “Why are you questioning me?” even though normally I’d just answer and move on.

It lasted several days, yeah. It wasn’t just one afternoon where I had coffee or got good news. It was more like a few days in a row where I felt unstoppable, and then over little things I’d get sharp with people in a way that didn’t really fit the situation.

doctor.intent: Determine the presence of manic episodes
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or elevated for several days in a row, without any apparent reason?

target_item.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Earlier in the month I felt almost lit up and unstoppable, then I’d snap at my mom or my supervisor over little questions that normally wouldn’t bother me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a distinct several-day period of unusually elevated or extremely happy mood without an apparent reason.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think that’s what I was trying to describe. Earlier this month, there were several days where I felt really elevated for no clear reason. Like nothing major had happened that would explain it — I hadn’t gotten some amazing news or anything — but I just felt kind of lit up, like I had this sense that I could handle everything and that I was almost unstoppable.

It wasn’t just “I’m having a nice day,” either. It felt bigger than that, like my mood was turned up too high. And at first it almost felt good, because I was more confident and energized in my head, but then it would switch really quickly into irritation. Like my mom would ask me a normal question, something that shouldn’t have bothered me at all, and I’d snap at her. Or my supervisor would ask me to clarify something, and I’d feel this immediate annoyance, like they were getting in my way or questioning me, even though normally I’d just answer.

So yes, it did feel elevated for several days, and I don’t think there was an obvious reason for it. It kind of came on like this charged feeling, and then I was more reactive than usual.

doctor.intent: Determine if patient's mood swings are a result of external factors
doctor.question: Do you think anything in particular triggers these mood swings of feeling really up or charged, and then crashing back down?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: The really obvious cycling between that charged-up stretch and this crash has been going on for about a month, since the mortgage became real.
target_item.reason: The question asks what might trigger the cycling between feeling charged-up and crashing; this item mentions that the obvious cycling has been going on since the mortgage became real, which is the closest listed context/trigger.

patient.answer:
I think the biggest thing I can point to is the mortgage. Like, once that became real — not just an idea or something we were talking about in the future, but actually real — that’s when I started noticing the more obvious cycling.

It’s been about a month, I’d say. Before that, I’m sure I had moods, obviously, but this more noticeable pattern of feeling really charged up and then coming back down hard… that seems like it started around then. It’s like my brain latched onto it as this huge life thing, and since then I’ve been going up and down in a way that feels much more obvious to me.

So I don’t know if it’s the only trigger, but that’s the main one I can identify. The mortgage becoming real feels like the point where this all got louder.

Yes. Earlier this month, there was definitely a stretch like that — at least several days in a row — where I felt… I don’t know, almost lit up. Like I had this extra push in me and I could do anything, or handle everything, and I remember thinking I felt kind of unstoppable.

Like my mom would ask me a small question, just normal stuff, and I’d snap at her like she was bothering me. Or at work, if my supervisor asked me to clarify something, I’d feel immediately annoyed, like they were criticizing me or slowing me down, even though looking back they were just asking a basic question.

So yes, it did last for several days, and it felt noticeably different from my normal mood.

Yes, that did happen. During that stretch I was talking about, there were several nights where I only slept maybe three or four hours, which is really not much for me, and then I’d still get up feeling strangely charged.

I’d wake up and feel like I was already switched on, like coffee wasn’t even necessary. I remember thinking it was weird because I knew I hadn’t slept enough, but my body didn’t feel like it was catching up to that. It was more like I was running on this internal energy, and I didn’t feel tired in the normal way.

patient.answer:
Yes… lately I have been feeling depressed, pretty much most days. I don’t know if I can neatly measure it, but it feels like I wake up and there’s already this heavy, empty feeling sitting in my chest before anything has even happened.

And the weirdest part is, I’ll be sitting in my own condo — something I worked so hard for, something I thought was supposed to make me feel proud or settled — and instead I just feel like crying. Like I’ll look around and think, “This should feel good, I should be happy here,” but it doesn’t land that way. It just feels heavy and kind of hollow.

So yes, there has been a stretch where it feels like that nearly every day.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's hypomanic episodes have caused significant distress or impairment
doctor.question: Have these mood swings and periods of high energy caused problems for you at work, in relationships, or in other areas of your life?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the mood swings and high-energy periods have caused problems in work, relationships, or other life areas, which directly matches functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Yes… it has. I mean, I’m still getting to work, so from the outside I probably look like I’m functioning okay, but I don’t feel like I’m doing as well as I should be.

At work, I’ve made mistakes I normally don’t make, especially with reconciliations. Like I’ll think I’m being really productive or that I’m catching everything, and then later there’ll be numbers that don’t line up, or I’ll realize I missed something obvious. It happened enough that my supervisor actually pulled me aside to talk about it, which was embarrassing because I’m usually pretty careful with that stuff. That’s kind of the part of my job where I’m supposed to be reliable.

And outside work, I’ve been pulling back from people. I used to go to salsa class, and I haven’t been going. I keep making excuses or just not responding because I don’t feel like myself, and I don’t want people noticing or asking what’s wrong. Same with friends — I’ll avoid plans, even if part of me knows seeing them might help. It just feels like too much to show up and pretend I’m normal.
